title: Abdullah bin Fazil and His Brothers

keywords: abdullah bin fazil and his brothers
full_text:
Abdullah bin Fazil was an honest, God-fearing sea captain of Basra who inherited three merchant vessels from his father, dividing them equally with his two elder brothers. His brothers, reckless and envious, squandered their ships and twice returned to him destitute. Twice Abdullah embraced them, opened his coffers, and purchased new ships for them without a word of reproach.

During a trade voyage to the uncharted City of Stone—where an ancient population had been petrified for their idolatry—Abdullah discovered the surviving princess, who had been preserved for her piety. They fell in love and agreed to wed.

Consuming jealousy seized the two brothers: one night on the high seas, they threw Abdullah and his bride into the dark waves and sailed away with the ship!

Abdullah and the maiden were washed ashore on an enchanted island. Through divine providence and his unshakeable faith, Abdullah befriended a gentle sea-spirit who carried them back to Basra.

When Abdullah arrived at his home, he found his two brothers arrested by the city magistrate for piracy and facing the scaffold.

Abdullah ran to the tribunal, threw his arms around his weeping brothers, and pleaded for their lives! He gave them a share of his recovered wealth and forgave them completely before all the people.

Overwhelmed by such saintly, superhuman mercy, the brothers repented with genuine tears, renounced their envy, and lived in peaceful brotherhood for the rest of their days, proving that true love overcomes the darkest malice.
moral: Pious patience and endless forgiveness towards ungrateful kin break the hardest curse of envy.
